correctness.rationale: For the balanced two-atom kernel, symmetry forces every scaling to remain scalar. Substituting a scalar incoming column scaling into the source certificate equations yields the exact feasible intermediate plan, zero repair defect, the displayed primal and dual bounds, and hence the closed certificate gap. The derivative of \(G\) is strictly negative for every \(p>0\); the asymptotic slack and exact stopping-index formulas then follow analytically. The packaged verifier only supplements these symbolic steps.

value.rationale: The finding gives a natural exact calibration point for a newly proposed anytime certificate. It decomposes the certificate into true entropic primal bias, explicit dual slack, and an identically zero repair contribution; proves the certificate becomes relatively sharp; and turns the source paper's empirical faster-cooling explanation into an exact asymptotic stopping law on the smallest nontrivial balanced instance. This is useful as a mathematical unit test and as a boundary case for future certificate analyses, while the limitations prevent extrapolation beyond the benchmark.
